name: Goblet Squat with Pause
description: The goblet squat with pause combines the upright-torso goblet squat position with a deliberate hold at the bottom. The pause eliminates the stretch-shortening reflex, forcing the quadriceps, glutes, and core to generate force from a dead stop. It is particularly effective for building squat positional strength in beginners and for improving hip mobility by using the pause position to open the hips.

execution.starting_position: Hold a dumbbell or kettlebell vertically at chest height with both hands cupping the top of the weight. Feet shoulder-width apart, toes pointed slightly out.
execution.setup_instructions: Same as the goblet squat setup. The weight held at the chest acts as a counterbalance, promoting a more upright torso.
steps: Step 1: Hold the weight at chest height. Core braced. Push the knees out over the toes.
Step 2: Descend to full depth — hips below knees if possible.
Step 3: Hold the bottom position for 2–5 seconds. Use the elbows to gently push the knees outward at the bottom. Breathe steadily.
Step 4: Drive through the entire foot to return to standing.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale before descent, breathe steadily through the pause, exhale on the ascent.
common_mistakes: Heels rising at the bottom — caused by insufficient ankle dorsiflexion
Lumbar rounding at depth — reduce weight or elevate heels slightly
Relaxing the knees inward during the pause
safety_considerations: If heels rise, place a small plate under them to elevate until ankle mobility improves
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full depth. The pause is at the deepest achievable position with neutral spine.
coaching_cues: Elbows push knees apart at the bottom
Stay tight in the pause — don't sit and relax
Drive up with your legs, not by leaning forward
